about: Where every account layout this checker reads was read, and what each program looked like on mainnet that day. deployedSlot is the program-data account's last deploy slot at the reading: a later slot on chain means the program moved after its layout was read, and the row that reads it says so.

bpf-upgradeable-loader.name: BPF Upgradeable Loader

layout.what: The program-data account's header (UpgradeableLoaderState::ProgramData: variant u32 = 3, slot u64, upgrade_authority_address as an option byte and 32 bytes; 45 bytes, size_of_programdata_metadata) and its address, seeds [program id]. Read to see whether a program was redeployed after its layout was read, and who may upgrade it

notes: Checked against the cluster's own parse of seven program-data accounts on 2026-10-13: the slot and authority recorded for each program below are the cluster's, and the tests hold this decoder to them.

layout.what: Mint (82 bytes: mint_authority COption 36, supply u64, decimals u8, is_initialized u8, freeze_authority COption 36) and Account (165 bytes: mint 32, owner 32, amount u64, delegate COption 36, state u8, is_native COption 12, delegated_amount u64, close_authority COption 36), from the Pack impls

The same Mint and Account bases padded to 165 bytes, one account-type byte, then type-length-value extensions (type u16, length u16); the ExtensionType numbering and the TransferFeeConfig, MintCloseAuthority, DefaultAccountState, NonTransferable, PermanentDelegate, TransferHook, MetadataPointer and PausableConfig structs

TokenMetadata, the metadata a Token-2022 mint may hold in itself (Borsh: update_authority as 32 bytes that are all zero when absent, mint, name, symbol, uri, additional_metadata as a list of string pairs)

The Metadata account (Borsh: key u8, updateAuthority, mint, data { name, symbol, uri, sellerFeeBasisPoints u16, creators option<vec<{ address, verified, share }>> }, primarySaleHappened bool, isMutable bool) and its address, seeds ["metadata", program, mint]

jupiter-lock.name: Jupiter Lock

layout.what: VestingEscrow, from the IDL the program publishes on chain (the account 2ntks693dfgHkYeyufFzV8jsf2QnEWoBbLHjXBE3WxWE, inflated). Vendored unchanged as idl/locker.json

What the two mode bytes mean (0 none, 1 creator only, 2 recipient only, 3 creator or recipient, for both cancel_mode and update_recipient_mode), the escrow address (seeds ["escrow", base]) and the token program flag (0 SPL Token, 1 Token-2022)

notes: The program repository Jupiter's developer page links (github.com/jup-ag/jup-lock) answered 404 on 2026-10-13: the program's own source could not be read. The IDL on chain and the SDK were.

Jupiter's page (docs.jup.ag/user-docs/launch/lock/how-it-works, read 2026-10-13): "These permissions are set once and cannot be changed after the lock is created." and "The Jupiter Lock program is upgradeable."

streamflow.name: Streamflow

layout.what: Contract and CreateParams (Borsh over fixed-size fields, no discriminator, 1104 bytes allotted), transcribed as idl/streamflow-contract.json

streamLayout (the same order, plus the two trailing fields fee_partner and cancel_request_time) and the offsets the SDK states itself (sender 49, recipient 113, mint 177, closed 671, old_metadata 714)

notes: The program was redeployed on 2026-09-21, three weeks after the newest public SDK commit. Its source is not public, so the layout is the SDKs' word. The tests hold it to real streams: the mint field must be the escrow token account's mint and the recipient's token account must be the recipient's.

Streamflow's developer page (developers.streamflow.finance/docs/core-concepts/streams/stream-lifecycle, read 2026-10-13): "The cancel and transfer flags can be toggled later via update(), but only if the stream was originally created with canUpdateRate: true." That is why can_update_rate fails row 7: a sender who may update may give itself the cancel and the transfer back.

meteora-damm-v2.name: Meteora DAMM v2 (cp_amm)

layout.what: Pool, Position, the three base-fee layouts, claim_position_fee's account order and EvtClaimPositionFee, from the SDK's IDL at the commit that synced it with cp_amm 0.2.4, the version deployed on 2026-09-08. Vendored unchanged as idl/cp_amm.json

What the IDL does not carry: the enums (BaseFeeMode 0 time linear, 1 time exponential, 2 rate limiter, 3 market cap linear, 4 market cap exponential; CollectFeeMode 0 both tokens, 1 token B only, 2 compounding; PoolStatus 0 enabled, 1 disabled; PoolType 0 permissionless, 1 customizable; ActivationType 0 slot, 1 timestamp), the delegate permission bits (3 ClaimPositionFee, 4 ClaimPositionFeeToOwner), who may swap before activation (pool_action_access/permissionless.rs), the fee formulas, and the sizes the source asserts (Pool 1104, Position 400)

notes: The IDL the program holds on chain (F1hSvutXSc9iAvB9bQPmjNDwiN2tCXzazTEEvDgNCBMa) is still 0.2.0 and differs in Pool and Position: it was not used. The SDK's newest IDL, 0.2.5 (79ebbfe, 2026-09-30), has the same types and instructions as 0.2.4 and is not deployed.

Meteora's own layout test (programs/cp-amm/src/tests/test_layout.rs) reads pool E8zRkDw3UdzRc8qVWmqyQ9MLj7jhgZDHSroYud5t25A7 as cliff 500000000, mode 1, 120 periods of 60, reduction 265. This checker's test reads the same account from its fixture and must find the same five numbers.

Two things the program lets Meteora's operators do to any pool, which no account of the pool shows: set_pool_status (disable swaps; permission SetPoolStatus) and update_pool_fees (a new base fee once the schedule has ended, the dynamic fee at any time; permission UpdatePoolFees). Rows 8 and 10 say so.
